chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from the one whom he mentioned, from Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him), from his father, from his grandfather (peace be upon them both), regarding the will of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) to Ali (peace be upon him).

'Do not go out alone on a journey, for Satan is with the one, and he is further away from the two. O Ali! Indeed, if a man travels alone, he is misguided, and the two are misguided, and the three are a group.' He said, 'And some of them reported: for travelling.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual and social significance of traveling alone versus in a group in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam Musa al-Kazim (AS) highlights the spiritual vulnerability of solitude, framing travel as a metaphor for the journey of life where companionship provides protection against misguidance. It reflects the Shia emphasis on communal solidarity and the practical wisdom of avoiding isolation, which is seen as a state of being 'lost' or 'deviating' (ghāw). The distinction between the solitary individual and the group underscores the importance of collective strength in maintaining spiritual and physical safety.

en.hubeali: H 14913 – A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from his father, from the one whom he mentioned: Abu Al-Hassan Musaasws has narrated from hisasws fatherasws, from hisasws grandfatherasws regarding the will of the Rasool Allahsaww to Aliasws:

‘Do not go out alone on a journey for the Satan<sup>la</sup> would be with the loner, and he<sup>la</sup> is (also) with the two but further away. O Ali<sup>asws</sup>! If the man travels alone he is misguided, and two are (also) misguided, and the three is a group’. He (the narrator) said, ‘And some of them are reporting: ‘For travelling’.
en.sarwar: 466. Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Qasim Bin Muhammad, and Ali Bin Muhammad Al-Qasany, from Suleyman Bin Dawood, from Hammaad Bin Isa, who has narrated the following: Abu Abdullah (a.s.) having said: ‘Luqman (as) advised his (as) son: ‘O my (as) son! Travel with your sword, and your slippers, and your turban, and your tent, and your water container, and your needle, and your threads, and your shoe-repair kit, and your provision of medicines which are beneficial for you and the one is with you. And be in concordance with your companion except if it is in the disobedience to Allah (azwj) Mighty and Majestic’.
